ending: The Baudelaires expose Gunther as Count Olaf and discover that Esme Squalor is his secret girlfriend and accomplice, a villain rather than a guardian, who has been helping his scheme all along. Their plan to rescue the Quagmire triplets, whom they found imprisoned at the bottom of the building's fake elevator shaft and then hidden among the auction lots, fails at the last moment: Olaf and Esme escape with the triplets smuggled away, and the Baudelaires cannot follow, leaving their friends' fate uncertain. Jerome Squalor, horrified to learn what his wife truly is but unwilling to face the danger of raising three hunted children, leaves both Esme and the guardianship, and the orphans are returned to Mr. Poe's charge. The Baudelaires end the book without their friends and without a home, but with a growing understanding that Olaf, Esme, and the mysterious V.F.D. are all bound together in a larger secret they are only beginning to glimpse.
in_short: The Baudelaires are placed with Jerome and Esme Squalor in a penthouse at 667 Dark Avenue, where fashion rules absolutely: because darkness is 'in,' the elevators sit dark and unused. Jerome is kind but avoids all conflict, and Esme is obsessed with what is stylish. When an auctioneer called Gunther arrives to run an 'In Auction,' the children recognize him as Count Olaf. Exploring the dark, out-of-service elevator, they discover it is a fake shaft, and at the bottom they find their kidnapped friends, the Quagmire triplets, caged. Rescue attempts go wrong, and the villains hide the Quagmires among the auction lots to smuggle them out of the city. At the auction the children uncover the plan, expose Gunther as Count Olaf, and learn that Esme is his accomplice, not merely a fashionable guardian. Olaf and Esme escape, carrying the Quagmires away to an unknown fate, and Jerome, unwilling to fight, gives up the children, who are left searching for their friends once more.

recaps.text: The Baudelaire orphans, inventor Violet, reader Klaus, and biting baby Sunny, lost their parents to a fire and were left a fortune held in trust. The banker Mr. Poe has moved them through a string of guardians, and each time the greedy actor Count Olaf, known by his single eyebrow and ankle tattoo, has pursued them in disguise, causing the deaths of kind Uncle Monty and fearful Aunt Josephine and scheming at a lumbermill, always escaping after the children exposed him. At a boarding school the orphans befriended the Quagmire triplets, Duncan and Isadora, fellow orphans with their own fortune in sapphires, only for Olaf to kidnap them and flee. As they were dragged away, the Quagmires shouted the mysterious letters V.F.D. Now the Baudelaires are placed with a new guardian, determined not only to survive Olaf but to rescue their captured friends and to learn what the secret V.F.D. means.

Mr. Poe places the Baudelaires with Jerome and Esme Squalor, a wealthy couple living in a penthouse at 667 Dark Avenue. Esme, the city's sixth most important financial advisor, is fanatically devoted to whatever is fashionable, and because darkness is currently 'in,' the building's elevators are kept dark and disused, so residents must climb dozens of flights of stairs. Jerome is warm and generous but pathologically unwilling to argue or take a stand. The children hope this new home may bring them closer to the kidnapped Quagmires, sensing Olaf's hand nearby. Their fears are confirmed when an auctioneer named Gunther, sporting a monocle and a fake foreign accent, arrives to organize an upcoming 'In Auction.' The Baudelaires recognize Gunther as Count Olaf in disguise and realize that a new scheme is unfolding in the fashionable building around them.

Investigating the strange, dark elevator, the Baudelaires discover that one of the elevators is a fraud, an 'ersatz' shaft with no car, dropping far below the building. Climbing down the shaft, they find their kidnapped friends, the Quagmire triplets, imprisoned in a cage at the bottom. Overjoyed but constrained, the children begin planning how to free Duncan and Isadora and smuggle them to safety, all while keeping their discovery hidden from Gunther and the adults. They come to suspect that the villains intend to use the coming auction to spirit the Quagmires out of the city, hidden among the many lots up for sale. Racing against the auction date, the Baudelaires work to rescue their friends before they can be shipped away, using Violet's inventiveness and Klaus's research to navigate the treacherous shaft and the strict fashions of the household.

The children's rescue efforts go awry, and the villains move the Quagmires, hiding them among the items to be sold at the In Auction so they can be carried off in plain sight. Studying the auction catalog, the Baudelaires try to work out which lot conceals their friends before it is sold and taken beyond reach. With the auction approaching and the household consumed by fashionable excitement, the orphans prepare a desperate plan to identify the right lot and free Duncan and Isadora at the event itself, even as Gunther and his allies tighten their control over the proceedings and the Baudelaires' chances of saving their friends grow slimmer.

At the In Auction the Baudelaires' plan unravels: the lot they hoped held the Quagmires does not, and the villains have concealed the triplets in a different item, which is carried off before the children can intervene. In the confrontation, the orphans expose Gunther as Count Olaf, and it is revealed that Esme Squalor is his secret accomplice and girlfriend, a villain who has been aiding his scheme rather than protecting the children. Olaf and Esme escape with the Quagmires, leaving their friends' fate unknown. Jerome, appalled to discover the truth about his wife but unwilling to face the dangers of guarding the hunted orphans, abandons both Esme and the guardianship. The Baudelaires are returned to Mr. Poe, once again without a home and without their friends, but more certain than ever that Olaf, Esme, and the mysterious V.F.D. are pieces of one larger secret.
